newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - July 11.

-- PENSIONS MIS-SELLING LEADS TO SURGE IN SALARIES

The rush to meet government deadlines for resolving the 4bn stg pensions mis-selling scandal has led to an acute shortage of staff amongst pension providers, causing a surge in salaries and extensive poaching. A survey conducted by Jonathan Wren, the financial recruitment consultants, shows that pension providers are in need of at least 25 per cent more staff if they are to resolve all cases by the end of next year.
-- WAIGEL CONFIDENT ABOUT EMU TARGET

Theo Waigel, the German finance minister, is today seeking approval from the cabinet for higher federal borrowing this year and a 1998 federal deficit that is only DM400m below its constitutional ceiling. Outlining the government's fiscal strategy to members of the governing coalition, Waigel said he was confident that public borrowing this year would not exceed more than the 3 per cent of the GDP, the specified requirement for entry into the EMU.
-- TRADING SCREENS ENCOURAGE PRIVATE BIDS

In the run up to the introduction of electronic trading, more and more British brokers and investors are using trading screens to make private bids and offers for large blocks of shares. The shift towards brokers sending private electronic messages in the dealing of shares could reduce the amount of business in the public "order driven" market due to be introduced on October 20.
-- FINANCIAL SERVICES HELP CUT TRADE DEFICIT

Record overseas earnings from the financial services sector helped to reduce the UK trade deficit last year according to statistics compiled by British Invisibles, the private sector body which promotes services abroad. Overseas earnings jumped by 2bn stg to 22.7bn in 1996, more than accounting for the reduction in the current account deficit of the UK's balance of payments last year.
-- MACHINE TOOL PRODUCTION FALLS BY 3.2 PER CENT

Britain is expected this year to suffer its first year-on-year fall in machine tool production. According to Cecimo, the European machine tool industry trade association European industry output will rise 2 per cent this year, with the UK seeing a fall in output mainly because of the strong pound.
-- GEC AND FINMECCANICA IN DEFENCE LINK

GEC and the Italian state owned Finmeccanica yesterday agreed Thursday to pool elements of their defence business. The outline agreement calls for their subsidiaries, GEC-Marconi and Alenia Difesia to create three joint ventures , with sales exceeding 2bn. They will cover missiles, radar, naval systems, avionics and guns and armoured vehicles.
-- SMITH & NEPHEW CHIEF IN HUNT FOR BIG ACQUISITIONS

Smith & Nephew, the UK's leading health care group,is seeking large strategic acquisitions to protect its position. Chief executive Chris O'Donnell has already made one approach and predicts consolidation in the medical devices industry. He said he was still awaiting a response from Roche regarding their bid to buy DePuy, the American artifcial limb maker.
-- GAZPROM HIT BY TAX PENALTIES

Huge financial penalties imposed on Gaxprom for late payment of taxes last year depressed net income at the giant Russian gas company t Rbs8,980bn (900m stg). In its first set of accounts prepared under international standards, Gazprom revealed yesterday that it had paid Rbs15,799bn (1.6bn) in penalties and interest due for late payment of bills in spite of being owed far more by its customers.
-- BANKS MAY FACE INTERNET ATTACK FROM OUTSIDER

Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover, the recently merged financial services group, is considering starting a direct banking business over the internet using the Discover credit card name. The move would be the first real competition to the traditional banking business from outside the sector. Up to now innovations in electronic banking have been established by leading commercial banks such as Wells Fargo and Citibank.
-- DULL PHONELINK LOOKS TO REVAMPED MANAGEMENT

UK electronic information service Phonelink saw its shares tumble on Thursday, as the group announced losses of 6.17m stg on turnover at 4.3m stg for the year to March 31st. Phonelink emphasised its balance sheet remained strong, with no debt and a cash level of over 9m stg. Finance director Richard Law stated the group will retain its focus on technology, commercial and marketing issues under new chief executive Graham Ramsey.
